caption:
True…but there’s a plot twist. 

According to Yale School of Medicine, during pregnancy, biological age increased by about 2 years. It makes sense. The sheer metabolic and physiological demands of growing a human naturally accelerates aging at the cellular level.⁠
⁠
But here’s the surprise. At three months postpartum, women’s biological age didn’t just stop increasing, it completely declined. For some, their biological age dropped by as much as 8 years compared to late pregnancy, which can be attributed to: ⁠
⁠
✨ Body Mass Index (BMI): Starting your pregnancy at a higher weight can make it harder for your cells to recover.⁠
⁠
✨ Breastfeeding: Exclusively breastfeeding can biologically fast-forward your recovery.⁠
⁠
The unknown: Lead researcher Kieran O’Donnell noted that they aren’t sure if the body is just returning to its pre-pregnancy baseline or if pregnancy leaves you biologically younger than when you started. ⁠
⁠
Only time will tell. ⁠

- Young adults are leading with remarkable clarity - only 50% drink now (down from 72% in 2004).

- Even drinkers are drinking dramatically less - only 24% had alcohol yesterday (record low), and the average is just 2.8 drinks per week.

Your liver processes alcohol as a toxin because that’s exactly what it is.

If you do choose to drink occasionally, see my other post on minimizing damage. But know this: 53% of Americans now understand that even “moderate” drinking is harmful - nearly double from 2015.

caption:
GRIP STRENGTH & LONGEVITY: “LIVE HANGS” 

Congratulations Ann Crile Esselstyn, who at *90 years and 231 days* old (title card says 93), did a continual bar grip hang for 2 minutes and 52 seconds. (And set a @guinnessworldrecords WR)

Grip strength and grip endurance (not exactly the same thing) are correlates of longevity. They are great to train for but grip strength alone does not extend life. So what do they reflect?

We often think about the muscle aspect of grip. To me,the really interesting data = the relationship between grip and longevity of *cognitive functioning*.

Why would there be a relationship there?

In neuroscience, we refer to the upper and the lower motor neurons. Upper motor neurons are in the brain and are involved in deliberate action (among other things); lower motor neurons are in the spinal cord and directly connect to the muscles by extending out of the central nervous system into the peripheral nervous system. They directly cause muscles to contract.

We also think about proximal muscles, which are the muscle muscles near the midline and distal muscles like those tips of your calves, forearms, fingers and toes.

Early but compelling evidence suggest that distal strength— the motor neuron control of the parts of your body furthest from your midline, is one of the first things to atrophy as you age. 

You can offset this with strong, gripping, keeping your feet, strong, calves, etc.

So while it’s important to train your core and the muscles of your legs, chest back and arms, don’t forget about feet yes feet! 

And hands and forearms. It’s not just about aesthetics. It’s very likely about maintaining those upper motor brain neurons. 

Once specific sets of neurons in the brain start to die off they often take others with them, the so-called bystander effect.

More on this in a Huberman Lab podcast to come but meanwhile, wherever you’re at in your fitness in longevity training the whole body and keep going! And congrats to Ann. That’s a super impressive timing at any age!

caption:
Syrniki reinvented😜
One of my favourite Slavic desserts is Syrniki. It is made with curd cheese. They usually give them a round, slightly flattened shape and fry them in the pan one by one, but I decided to give Syrniki a European touch and baked them in cupcake cases in the oven. Less hassle, more enjoyment😉 

The recipe is very easy. The only thing is the curd cheese itself which you can buy only in Slavic shops in London. Brits don't usually have it.
I bought 2 packs (250gr each) of Polish curd cheese, they call it twarog, which is the same in other Slavic languages. 1 egg, 3-4 tb. spoons of erythritol (I don't use sugar any more to keep my blood sugar levels normal), 3 tb. spoons of oat flour, and a dash of vanilla syrup. Mix it with a blender, and that's it!
Then you just put the mixture into the cupcake cases and bake in the oven(180° for 25 mins). Take them out and let to cool down. Turn them over and serve with any topping. My fav is soured cream. This recipe makes 12 syrniks. Enjoy! 😁😋😊✨️✨️
Переосмысление сырников😜
Один из моих любимых славянских десертов — сырники. Он готовится из творога. Обычно им придают круглую, слегка приплюснутую форму и обжаривают на сковороде по одному, но я решила придать сырникам европейский колорит и запекла их в формочках для кексов в духовке. Меньше хлопот, больше удовольствия😉 

Рецепт очень простой. Единственное, что нужно — это сам творог, который можно купить только в славянских магазинах в Лондоне. У британцев его обычно нет.
Я купила 2 пачки (по 250 г) польского творога, его называют twarog, что то же самое и в других славянских языках. 1 яйцо, 3-4 ст. ложки эритритола (я больше не использую сахар, чтобы поддерживать нормальный уровень сахара в крови), 3 ст. ложки овсяной муки и немного ванильного сиропа. Смешиваю блендером, и все!
 Затем просто положите смесь в формочки для кексов и выпекайте в духовке (180° в течение 25 минут). Достаньте их и дайте остыть. Переверните и подавайте с любой начинкой. Мой любимый вариант — сметана. По этому рецепту получается 12 сырников. Наслаждайтесь! 😁😋😊✨️✨️

caption:
As most of you are likely aware, last weekend it was announced that former President Joe Biden had been diagnosed with stage 4 (i.e., metastatic) prostate cancer. Putting politics and conspiracy theories aside, and speaking strictly from a medical perspective, the news is nothing short of a tragic demonstration of Medicine 2.0 at its worst.

Prostate cancer is one of the very few forms of cancer for which metastasis, and therefore mortality, are almost entirely preventable. Thus, news of such advanced disease in anyone is unacceptable in my mind. But the fact that this occurred in a man who presumably was receiving the best possible medical care — a man whose health had, until recently, been a matter of national security — underscores a bitter truth: despite our ability to catch and treat prostate cancer well before it spreads, this form of cancer remains the second leading causing of cancer deaths among men. Around 35,000 men die of prostate cancer each year in the United States alone, and most of those deaths are preventable. Tragic indeed.

As such, I’d like to take this high-profile case as an opportunity to try to make some small dent in those numbers. In this video, I explain why prostate cancer still contributes to so many unnecessary deaths and what you can do to prevent yourself or your loved ones from becoming part of those terrible statistics someday. In addition to the video, I have summarized some of these points in-text in this week’s newsletter.

caption:
MUCH OF LEARNING (IN DOGS & HUMANS) IS TOP DOWN INHIBITION •

Much of learning involves adjusting the connections between the prefrontal cortex and deeper brain structures that control impulses. Indeed, if you look at motor learning in humans or other mammals, you’ll notice that most of building a skill is about eliminating incorrect aspects of a movement.

This is my second bulldog mutt, and as with the last one (Costello) I started the training early at 9 weeks. 

Strummer is doing a great job learning to suppress his impulse to move aka “sit” and to come when called, to stay calm around food and all the rest. 

Dogs have a tiny prefrontal cortex relative to humans but they can multipurpose it to learn lots of things and lots of different scenarios. They are oh so smart. But it is kind of fun to think about how they’re training you as well.

Indeed training a bulldog breed (because they’re so stubborn) is also about training yourself in patience. Strummer is part mastiff and boxer/pit too but he’s still been giving us a run for our money on the patience side! What he doesn’t know is I’ve done this before. And it’s been pure pleasure.

NOTE: I want to be thoughtful in sharing any post about a bulldog and how great they are because they have wonderful personalities, but they are not trivial to raise properly and take care of properly so if you decide to take that on understand it will take many hours per day or more to train them up and to keep them healthy. If they’re just allowed to sleep and you let them just kind of move around like sea turtles they get very unhealthy and unhappy. 

I suggest getting a mutt because they tend to be a little bit easier, but then they’ll also have more energy. So then you’ve got a stubborn high energy dog! But they have huge hearts, like no other breed (in my opinion). 

We can learn a lot from dogs. And other animals and our interactions w/them -not just observing them.

Plastic blenders are a source of microplastics that most people overlook.

Those with plastic jars or pitchers release microplastics, and even nanoplastics, into blended food or drinks due to friction and mechanical abrasion during blending.

BPA-free products are safer but can still release particles due to heavy use, heat, or abrasion. My advice is to switch to a completely stainless-steel blender. It’s the only way to avoid contamination.

But that does not mean all randomized studies on seed oils are unreliable - randomization is specifically used to reduce hidden factors, and when randomized trials, cohort studies, and major reviews broadly point the same way, that carries more weight than just assuming unseen confounders. 5. You can find studies claiming seed oils are harmful, but the key question is what the higher-quality evidence says overall, and large reviews and major heart-health bodies have generally not concluded that normal seed oil intake is uniquely inflammatory or harmful; they more often find benefit when unsaturated fats replace saturated fats!!! This proverb is as simple as it gets: eat wrong, and no drug can fix you. Eat right, and you won't need one at all.

Think about it this way. Your body is like a car. You can take it to the mechanic every week — but if you keep putting the wrong fuel in the tank, it's going to keep breaking down. The mechanic isn't the problem. The fuel is.

Food is information. Every single bite you take is sending instructions to your body — telling it to repair or break down, to fight inflammation or feed it, to age slowly or fast. 

The Sardinian shepherds I studied while writing Young Forever weren't taking a handful of supplements or managing a list of prescriptions. They were eating wild, seasonal, phytochemical-rich food their whole lives. Their bodies simply had what they needed to keep running.

Most of us have it backwards. We wait until something breaks, then look for a pill to fix it. But medicine was always meant to be the last resort — not the plan.

Food is the plan.

caption:
This is a big deal. Omega-3s reduce aggressive behavior across randomized controlled trials.

A meta-analysis of 29 studies and nearly 4,000 participants found that omega-3 supplementation reduced aggressive behavior by up to 28%. The benefit was broadly consistent across children and adults, males and females, community and clinical samples, and across high and low omega-3 doses and treatment durations. It also helped with both reactive/impulsive and proactive/planned aggression.

Mechanistically, this makes sense. Omega-3s are deeply involved in brain cell membranes, neurotransmission, neuroinflammation, cerebral blood flow, and gene regulation. DHA is especially enriched in the prefrontal cortex, which is critical for impulse control, emotion regulation, and executive function.

The authors even concluded that there is now “sufficient evidence” to begin implementing omega-3 supplementation to reduce aggression in the community, the clinic, or the criminal justice system. That’s a remarkable statement for a nutritional intervention and a reminder that omega-3s influence brain health and may also shape behavior in meaningful ways.

Study title:
“Omega-3 supplementation reduces aggressive behavior: A meta-analytic review of randomized controlled trials”

caption:
DO TELL. NO EXPLANATION NEEDED (BUT FEEL FREE TO ELABORATE IF YOU WANT) •
-
A new year is not just another day and trip around the sun. A unique feature of the human brain is that we don’t just hold memories of past and perceive things in the present, we can anticipate things far into the future and carry out plans according to how we think we’ll feel in the future. 
-
New Year’s resolutions are good example of us segmenting time and making plans. 
-
I think that’s great. I add one “do more of X” and one “eliminate Y”, each year. (Sometimes several of each, and I write them down, and I check back at the end of the year to see if I held up to it.) 
-
I was struck by a post from @danielpink who’s an expert in the data on behavioral change. He mentioned that one word thematic titles about a new year and what we want from ourselves in that year can have a bigger impact than an unframed list of changes, but it’s good to have a list of specific changes as well. 
-
Apparently a one word thematics can help frame it all and keep you on track. That makes sense; we all get busy… within a few weeks everyone will be talking about Valentine’s Day or whatever and the notion that we’re in a new year seems to vanish. Returning to a one word theme is doable.
-
So… I’m on board this one word thematic idea even if it’s just to remind us of the specific changes to make. 
-

Most people think liver issues come from alcohol.

But one of the most common liver conditions in the US has nothing to do with your favorite cocktail.

It’s called metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MΑSLD)—and nearly 1 in 3 adults has it.

One of the biggest drivers: drinking diet sodas and sugary drinks.

The problem? Early MASLD rarely shows symptoms, so it can be easy to miss.
That’s why deeper testing of liver function, metabolic health, and systemic inflammation matters.

Test & track:
- Liver stress: ALT, AST, GGT, ALP
- Metabolic health: Glucose, Insulin, HbA1c
- Inflammation levels: hs-CRP

MASLD isn’t an alcohol problem.
It develops from patterns over time. 

The good news? Early detection and healthy habits can go a long way toward preventing or possibly even reversing MASLD.

caption:
Did you know this?

The field of sociogenomics shows that your internal state can influence how your genes are expressed, especially those involved in inflammation and immune function.

When the brain perceives ongoing stress, whether from external pressures or persistent negative thought patterns, it activates the body’s stress response. This increases cortisol and inflammatory signaling, which can shift gene expression toward a more inflammatory state.

Over time, this pattern, known as the conserved transcriptional response to adversity, is linked to a higher risk of chronic disease.

On the other hand, when the nervous system is more regulated, through practices like mindfulness, movement, quality sleep, and social connection, the body sends different signals. These can help reduce inflammatory gene activity and support repair and resilience.

Your brain and body are in constant communication.

And the signals you send every day matter.

The next frontier in medicine isn’t another drug.

It’s a radical shift in how we view the body, the brain, and disease itself.

The answer is in how we eat, move, sleep, connect, and live. It’s in our soil, our food system, our communities, our kitchens.

The next revolution in medicine will come not from the lab but from returning to the root.

Supplementing with protein during strength training can increase gains in muscle size by approximately 27%, even when baseline protein intake is already considered adequate.

В моем профиле вы могли видеть, что я практикую Рейки. Хочу вам сообщить, что я убираю модальность Рейки из описания своей деятельности.
Сейчас объясню почему. Мои руки и моя энергетика имеют свойство исцелять, убирать боль, снимать напряжение в теле, приносить ясность в сознание и убирать энергетические блоки. Так было всегда, сколько я себя помню. С раннего детства мои руки были горячие, мне было жарко в варежках в самую холодную зиму и я их скидывала.
У моего папы были такие руки, видимо передалось от него. Мы с ним по очереди помогали маме при ее сильнейших мигренях, когда лекарства ее не спасали. Мы просто массировали ей голову, думали боль проходит от массажа. Но это было свойство нашей энергии на самом деле.
Я никогда не знала про Рейки. Когда переехала в Лондон, случайно увидела книгу одного мастера Рейки и узнала про такой вид энергопрактики. Оказалось, он живёт в 5 остановках метро от меня. Конечно же я поехала к нему. Оказалось, что тут есть целая академия неизвестного мне до того момента какого-то Рейки, которую он создал. Я записалась на обучение. Там учили тому, что я умела делать интуитивно. Единственное, что было для меня новое - это работа на дистанции. Вот это было круто! В последствии, у меня были клиенты аж в Австралии. Работа на дистанции так же эффективна как и напрямую. Все это происходило еще в 2017 году.

THE ONE HEALTH PROTOCOL THAT MAKES ALL THE REST FAR EASIER: SPIKE YOUR CORTISOL IN THE 1ST HOUR OF YOUR DAY •
-
Guess what, whether you are male or female, young or old you want your morning cortisol high (yes high) and your nighttime cortisol low. That is what’s going to establish healthy metabolism, focus, excellent sleep, best stress control, even heightened ability to learn and longevity. 
-
Deliberately spiking your morning cortisol the way I describe in this video will help you have low cortisol in the final hours before sleep, and will vastly improve your sleep. And as we all know, high-quality sleep is the foundation of mental health, physical health, and performance. 
-
Cortisol has gotten a bad rap.  It’s healthy function is to wake you up each morning. It’s literally called. The cortisol awakening response. And if you don’t spike your cortisol in the first hours of your day, you make yourself vulnerable to cortisol increases later in the day, more stress and hormone dysregulation as well as sleep disturbances.
-
Also: if you are a regular drinker of caffeine, know that it does not increase cortisol. 
-
Also this: deliberate cold exposure does not increase cortisol! The best studies show the exact opposite! 
-
In this video, I explain simple zero cost things you can do to get your cortisol rhythm correct. Viewing bright light ideally from sunlight in the first hour of your day is going to be the most potent tool for that, but after an hour post waking that window closes at least until the next morning. 10K Lux artificial light is helpful if you can’t access sunlight.
-
Put your questions in the comments section below this post.

WHAT HAPPENS IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW YOUR DREAMS •

My guest on the Huberman lab podcast out now is Steven Pressfield, author of numerous best selling books and screenplays. We discussed how to overcome resistance and procrastination using practical tools, not mantras or inspirational language.
-
Steven wrote his first book at 52 (!) and at 82 is still incredibly mentally and physically vigorous (!) He resistance trains 5 days a week at 4:45 AM, and approaches his writing with the same rigor. 2 hours a day every day. No exceptions.
-
Here we are discussing what happens if you do not pursue your dreams. And while that might seem like a luxury, there are numerous accounts of people finding an hour or two per day to write or draw or do things to build out their creative dreams.
-
His point is not meant to scare people into doing what they love, but rather to consider seriously what they most want and to make the pockets of time to pursue that. 
-
His point that the energy we are endowed with to make our own unique contribution to the world is a sort of divine energy is one I subscribe to… and I agree that if we don’t channel it correctly, it can end up being destructive.

caption:
The current physical activity guidelines are too low.

I’ve been saying this for a while. And a new study confirms it.

Meeting the standard 150 minutes/week was associated with only a modest ~8–9% lower cardiovascular risk.

The biggest protection occurred at roughly 560–610 minutes/week, about 3–4× higher, where cardiovascular risk was 30% lower.

One other interesting finding was that people with a higher cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 max) needed less activity than people with lower fitness to achieve the same reduction in risk!

We need to distinguish between the minimal activity volume required for basic protection, and the substantially higher volumes required for optimal resilience.

caption:
Sitting on the ground more is one of the simplest things you can do for long-term mobility.

It sounds almost too basic, but getting down to the floor and back up is a real marker of independence. If you lose that ability, a lot of everyday function starts to go with it.

Sit with your legs straight out. Sit cross-legged. Kneel. Shift around. These positions gently restore hip rotation, ankle mobility, and the ability to move your body in and out of different shapes.

This kind of low-level, daily movement practice helps maintain better joint mechanics, and according to @thereadystate, it might be one reason why “floor cultures” such as those in Asia often preserve mobility longer and have fewer problems related to stiffness and loss of function.

caption:
“FACE PULLS”: SET YOUR DEFAULT POSTURE UPRIGHT, MAKE YOUR SHOULDERS AND NECK STABLE •

This week’s Huberman Lab podcast features Jeff Cavalier of  @athleanx — he’s a licensed physical therapist, strength and conditioning coach known for helping people reach their fitness goals, overcoming pain and injury with specific movements and getting tremendous longevity from their fitness training. 

We sat down and talked about “the little things that allow you to do the big important things for your entire life” on the podcast. 

Yes it’s true: You need to do the basics. Men and women should do basic compound movements of pressing and pulling and for their legs …and do so with progressive resistance. Every week. 

But the issue people tend to run into is pain or injuries or challenges with imbalanced mechanics. Doing certain little things for just a few minutes per week can be the difference between lifelong pain-free training, great posture (at default— without having to think about it!) better breathing, better mobility, and on and on.

One of the key movements that every man and woman should do a few times a week at least are “face pulls” which is where you pull a rope from slightly above high-level on a cable machine (or you could use bands if you don’t have access to a cable machine) starting from a position where your hands are almost touching directly in front of you (arms straight) to what sort of looks like a “double biceps flexed pose”, but with your thumbs pointed back and  bit out & away from your ears. That’s the correct “external rotation” you want, which is essential… you can learn more about on the podcast. 

All the texting and sitting that we do nowadays has most people defaulting to internal rotation, chin down and C shaped… not good (for many reasons!).

A video of how to do face pulls correctly as well as train your arms correctly are available at the “Huberman lab clips” channel on You Tube. There is a short excerpt of it here as well.

Thank you, Jeff for being such a tremendous coach in public educator helping people get and stay super fit. We appreciate you!

Мы разучились принимать это состояние. Нам очень хочется побыстрее от него избавиться. Во что бы то ни стало устранить дискомфорт любыми способами. Я говорю о дискомфорте эмоциональном. Волнение, страх, тревогу, тоску и прочее - все это ну прям никак не хочется испытывать.

Современный человек с трудом смиряется с тем, что в жизни так или иначе происходят события, которые вызывают у нас не вполне приятные ощущения. Мы хотим, чтоб их просто не было. Но так не бывает. И вот когда что-то такое происходит, нас просто захлестывают негативные состояния, и почва уходит из под ног.

Современный человек стал очень хлипким в плане эмоциональной устойчивости.

Вот вчера на сессии мы с клиентом пытались учиться справляться с сильнейшим волнением перед экзаменами (это уже не первый такой запрос, с которым ко мне приходят, и молодёжь и взрослые). Ну просто "выносит" человека, стоит ей только подумать и представить как она идет на экзамен.

WANT TO LEARN FASTER? UNDERSTANDING HOW NEUROPLASTICITY WORKS IS THE KEY & IT INVOLVES 4 (actually 5) CRITICAL STEPS •
-
ALL learning involves neuroplasticity, and while a lot has been discussed about this topic, most of what you see misses the mark in one or several ways.
-
To learn, 1) you need to be alert, and 2) you need to be focused. But those are just prerequisites. They are necessary, but not sufficient for learning. The critical step that triggers the actual rewiring of brain circuits that causes “learning” is… 3) ERRORS.
-
Errors and often the emotional frustration that accompanies them is what signals to your nervous system that something needs to change. It’s critical that you internalize that fact! It makes logical sense if you think about it. Why would your nervous system change if it could perform everything that you’re trying to do?
-
4) Actual circuit remodeling underlying learning occurs during sleep, in particular during rapid eye movement sleep (REM).
-
And then there’s the additional critical feature that most people overlook and that’s 5) mental reflection on the learning process and in particular self testing for what you did correctly and what you did incorrectly.
-
In fact, the data on how best to study and learn all point to self testing as an incredibly valuable, but under used tool.
-
In this post, I discussed the practical steps to trigger and enhance learning. I also discussed how to accelerate learning and how to make it more durable over time. It’s 4 key steps. (And one additional one to boost learning).
-
Perhaps test yourself and see if you can remember what those 4-5 steps are… if you can’t don’t worry, go back and read it again. Yes this is an example of what I’m trying to explain. But once it’s locked in, you’ll never forget it.

caption:
A “plastic-free diet” can cut endocrine-disrupting chemicals in the body by up to 60% in just 1 week.

Participants in a recent study switched to low-plastic food, plastic-free kitchenware, and screened personal care products for 7 days.

Urinary BPA fell by 59%, and phthalates fell by up to 54%. Even switching personal care products alone significantly lowered MnBP, another phthalate, by 35%.

These chemicals have been linked to male and female reproductive problems, altered neurodevelopment in children, and even insulin resistance and cardiovascular disease.

The takeaway here is that exposure to plastic is not fixed or unavoidable. Reducing highly processed foods, canned foods, plastic packaging, and plastic contact during food prep and storage, as well as personal hygiene products that contain phthalates, can rapidly lower your internal burden of these chemicals.

Study title: Low-plastic diet and urinary levels of plastic-associated phthalates and bisphenols: the randomized controlled PERTH Trial

caption:
Muscle loss with age is common, but much of that decline is driven by inactivity, not aging alone.

On average, we reach peak muscle mass somewhere between 20 and 30, then lose about 8% per decade after that. By the time many adults reach their 70s and 80s, they may have only 60–80% of the muscle mass they had at 30.

A big reason why is anabolic resistance. As we get older, muscle becomes less responsive to amino acids, one of the key signals for building and maintaining muscle.

This is where resistance training becomes non-negotiable. It’s one of the main signals that tells muscle to grow. And just as importantly, it helps re-sensitize muscle to amino acids, so the body responds to protein more like it did when you were younger.

caption:
Is your breakfast making you eat more food throughout the day?

My friend Dr. David Ludwig at Harvard ran a fascinating study — he took teenage boys and gave them three breakfasts with the exact same calories: oatmeal, steel-cut oats, or an omelette.

The oatmeal group had sky-high levels of insulin and adrenaline — the same stress response your body has when being chased by a predator. And they ate 81% more food than the omelette group.

Steel-cut oats were better — but still led to 53% more calories consumed.

When you start your day with starch or sugar — oatmeal, a bagel, a muffin, pancakes, even a fruit smoothie — you’re setting yourself up for overeating for the rest of the day.

Your body doesn’t know the difference between a bowl of oatmeal and a stress response.

Start your morning with protein and fat. It’s one of the simplest things you can do to take control of your hunger, your hormones, and your energy.

caption:
Drink your coffee black (no additives) if you want the full health benefits. ☕️

2-3 cups per day has been associated with a 25% reduction in all-cause mortality. That benefit goes away when cream and/or sugar are added.

I think this happens for a few reasons:

• Dairy proteins can bind to coffee’s antioxidants and polyphenols and slow their absorption.

• Heavy cream, butter, and MCT-heavy coffee don’t necessarily block coffee polyphenols, but they can add substantial saturated fat and calories. For someone watching ApoB or LDL-C, this can work against the very cardiovascular benefits they’re hoping to get from coffee.
